title: Rams roll Cardinals without top receivers, surge into bye week with fourth straight win
content:
GLENDALE, Ariz. — The Los Angeles Rams scored two touchdowns in the final 1:06 of the second quarter to build a halftime lead and roll over the Arizona Cardinals 34-6 at State Farm Stadium on Sunday.

With the victory, the Rams improve to 6-4 as they head into their bye week on a four-game winning streak. The Cardinals fall to 3-7.

Matthew Stafford threw three touchdown passes, including a 22-yarder to wide receiver Xavier Smith after Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck threw an interception with 43 seconds remaining in the first half. The pass was picked off by safety Kam Kinchens, who returned it 33 yards and set the Rams up for the score.

Early in the third quarter, the Rams stormed downfield on an eight-play, 78-yard drive that was capped with a 1-yard plunge by running back Blake Corum, who scored a touchdown for the sixth straight game. Corum finished with 17 carries for 100 yards, the second 100-yard rushing game of his career.

Beck was picked off for a second time on the ensuing drive, and Stafford capitalized five plays later with a 19-yard strike to tight end Davis Allen, effectively putting the game away.

Without his top two receivers, Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, Stafford completed passes to nine different pass catchers. He finished 18-of-26 for 249 yards, those three touchdowns and an interception.

The Rams will come out of their bye with a brutal three-game stretch against the Green Bay Packers, Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers. The Cardinals have a road matchup in Kansas City next week.

It didn’t look great at the start, when the Cardinals were stacking the box and run-blitzing. The Rams pivoted to more pass attempts, only to lose their top two centers during the game, with a backup left guard already in. But in true Rams form, Stafford found his rhythm at the end of the first half, and everything looked different from there.

The biggest shift was the way Corum took over with elite vision, patience and cuts. That put the Rams in favorable downs and distances, unlocked play-action and left the receivers as the forgotten men, and all of a sudden four different wideouts — Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith — ripped off 20-yard gains.

I’m not convinced this is enough against a really good opponent, but it’s what they needed now with hopes of getting Davante Adams and Terrance Ferguson back soon. — Nate Atkins, Rams reporter

It’s been a big shift. Donald has had a much better season than his stats indicate, with consistent pressure and rerouting of run plays. But the double-teams that came his way for a month and a half were taking a toll on his 35-year-old back.

Now, Donald can rush in tandem with Garrett as the two move all around the Rams’ line to create mismatches and confusion. Donald finally got his first sacks of the season in this one, but he essentially had sack assists on two of Garrett’s last week.

With Trent McDuffie back, this defense is looking like the terrifying unit we thought it could be entering the season. It still has to show it against a good offense, though, which the Washington Commanders and Carson Beck-led Cardinals are not. — Atkins

Evaluating Beck’s NFL debut depends on your expectations coming in. Context matters. Because of injuries, the Cardinals were stretched thin at receiver, relying on those who previously played on special teams or the practice squad. They operated with a beat-up line that included a third-string center who made his first NFL start at the position.

Given the circumstances, Beck was OK.

The Cardinals are looking for their QB of the future, but this will be a slow burn. Starting with Sunday’s game against the Rams, Beck has eight games to prove he is worthy of beginning next season as QB1. Sunday marked the first game Beck has played since Arizona’s preseason opener on Aug. 6. He wasn’t going to tear it up, especially against the Rams.

The best part: Beck did not look overwhelmed. He didn’t battle the play clock. He went through his progressions. He threw a gorgeous 31-yard completion to receiver Devin Duvernay that ranked among the best passes any Arizona quarterback has thrown this season. He also tried to force a pass through the middle to running back Tyler Allgeier that was intercepted, and he lost a fumble while running for a first down.

This will likely continue for a while. If Beck improves — and the offense improves around him — the Cardinals may have something here. After one game, it’s much too early to tell. — Doug Haller, senior writer

This was an absolute must-win for the Rams given how daunting their upcoming schedule is and how the NFC West race was slipping away. If this team couldn’t get a win against the Cardinals this season, they just weren’t going to be a playoff team.

What helps is how smooth and dominant this performance was. It allowed the Rams to just get out with a win as more injuries piled up on the offensive line.

They’ll get an abbreviated bye week now before a Wednesday game against the Green Bay Packers on Thanksgiving Eve, but they need to find a way to get one or both of Ferguson and Adams back for that game, as it is starting to feel like a de facto playoff game with how the wild-card race is shaping up. — Atkins
